Composing steps into chains

Source: vignettes/compose.Rmd
compose.Rmd

A recipe such as needle is a fixed sequence of stages: segment the document, rank the chunks, read the best. When you want a sequence of your own, with a check after the answer or a step that rewrites the question, you build it from steps and run the steps in order as one arm. The arm is an ordinary hr_arm(), so hr_benchmark() compares it with recipes and with other chains on the same labelled questions, as vignette("compare") does for recipes.

Everything here runs offline on a stand-in model.

library(harnessr)
old <- gr_options(verbose = FALSE, embedder = "lexical")
cl <- gr_mock_client(function(messages, params) {
  if (grepl("You grade one response", messages[[1]]$content, fixed = TRUE)) {
    return('{"verdict": "pass", "reason": "It gives the figure."}')
  }
  "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars."
})
ref <- gr_qa_reference(
  questions = c(revenue = "What was revenue in 2024?"),
  documents = gr_example(), answers = list("45.2 million"), split = "test")

Steps

A step is a function of (input, ctx) that does one part of a run. gr_step() builds the document stages, "ingest", "segment" and "read", and gr_step_retrieve() builds a step that ranks the chunks and keeps the best without asking for an answer. Their settings are the ones the stage’s spec takes, and they are checked when the step is built:

gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 4)
#> <gr_step> retrieve (retrieve): top_k=4
try(gr_step("read", reader = "no_such_reader"))
#> Error in registry_get("readers", spec$reader, "readers", state = gr_state) : 
#>   Unknown reader 'no_such_reader'. Registered: ensemble, extract, hierarchical, iterative, map_reduce, preview, refine, rerank, retrieve, screen, skim, stuff.

hr_step() builds a step of your own. Inside a chain, ctx is the context hr_benchmark() gives an arm (its client, trace, judge and note shortcuts, and params), with the step’s name in ctx$step and its settings in ctx$step_params. This one grades the answer with a model and records the verdict as a signal of the run:

judge <- hr_step("judge", function(a, ctx) {
  j <- ctx$judge(a$answer, mode = "grade", reference = "45.2 million",
                 rubric = "Does it give the figure?", orders = 1)
  ctx$note("judged", j$verdicts$verdict[1])
  a
}, input = "answer", output = "answer")

input and output declare what a step takes and returns: "document", "doc", "chunks", "answer" or "state". They are optional, and hr_chain() uses them to check the order of the steps.

Chains

hr_chain() runs its steps in order: the first gets the item, each later step gets what the step before returned, and the chain returns what the last step returns. An argument’s name is the step’s name in the chain.

checked <- hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"),
                    retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 4),
                    read = gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"),
                    judge = judge, name = "checked")
checked
#> <hr_arm checked> version 0.0.1
#>   params: retrieve.top_k = 4, read.reader = stuff 
#>   hash: 4cb127da751d

The arm records each step’s settings as "step.setting", so a benchmark gets a param.retrieve.top_k column for it. A chain is derived from another by naming steps: NULL drops one, a step under an existing name replaces it where it stands, and a step under a new name is added at the end.

nojudge <- hr_chain(checked, judge = NULL, name = "nojudge")
wider <- hr_chain(checked, retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 8), name = "wider")
names(attr(wider, "hr_steps"))
#> [1] "segment"  "retrieve" "read"     "judge"

The three run side by side like any arms. Each run sends its requests at its own draw, so a cache does not hand one run’s reply to the next:

bench <- hr_benchmark(list(checked, nojudge, wider), ref, runs = 5, client = cl,
                      scorer = gr_scorer_answer())
aggregate(correct ~ arm + param.retrieve.top_k, bench, mean)
#>       arm param.retrieve.top_k correct
#> 1 checked                    4       1
#> 2 nojudge                    4       1
#> 3   wider                    8       1
head(hr_signals(bench, "judged")[, c("arm", "run", "item", "value")], 3)
#>       arm run    item value
#> 1 checked   1 revenue  pass
#> 2 checked   2 revenue  pass
#> 3 checked   3 revenue  pass

What a chain checks when it is built

A step that takes chunks when no step before it returns chunks warns with class hr_chain_gap: a read step would cut the document at the default settings without saying so. A segment step first in a chain does not warn, though it reads the document at the default ingest settings; put an ingest step before it to choose them. After a step that returns the answer, only steps that take "answer" or "state", or declare nothing, can follow.

tryCatch(hr_chain(read = gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"), name = "gap"),
         hr_chain_gap = function(w) conditionMessage(w))
#> [1] "Chain 'gap': step 'read' takes chunks, but no step before it returns them, so it will cut the document into chunks at the default settings. Add a segment step before it to choose them."
try(hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"), read = gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"),
             retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(), name = "late"))
#> Error in chain_check_order(steps, what) : 
#>   Chain 'late': step 'retrieve' takes "chunks", but it comes after step 'read', which returns the answer. After an answer only steps that take "answer" or "state" can follow.

Step names cannot contain a dot, since settings are named "step.setting", and cannot repeat.

When two chains are the same

A chain’s configuration is a hash of its steps’ code, the values that code reads, and their resolved settings. Two chains with the same configuration send the same requests, and hr_benchmark() warns (hr_same_config) when asked to compare them. A setting given at its default gives the same configuration as the setting left out:

a <- hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"), retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(), name = "a")
b <- hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"), retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 6),
              name = "b")
identical(attr(a, "hr_config"), attr(b, "hr_config"))
#> [1] TRUE
